hints: Focus on what you actually know here, you have p, V, T and mass, so this is an ideal gas molar mass puzzle.
Use $pV = nRT$ to find the moles of gas, remembering to convert $200 \text{ cm}^3$ to $2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$ and $101 \text{ kPa}$ to $101000 \text{ Pa}$.
Divide the mass $0.68 \text{ g}$ by your moles to get $M_r$ in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$, then match it to the familiar $A_r$ values of the gases listed.
walkthrough:
**Find the moles with the ideal gas equation**

We know pressure, volume and temperature, so we can find n directly. Remember SI units are essential for this equation.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$pV = nRT \text{ so } n = \frac{pV}{RT}$$

**Put the numbers in with correct units**

Convert volume and pressure: $V = 200 \text{ cm}^3 = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3$, $p = 101 \text{ kPa} = 101000 \text{ Pa}$, $T = 300 \text{ K}$, $R = 8.31 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$n = \frac{101000 \times 2.0 \times 10^{-4}}{8.31 \times 300} = \frac{20.2}{2493} \approx 0.00810 \text{ mol}$$

**Calculate the molar mass and identify the gas**

Molar mass links the weighed mass to the moles you just found. A value near 84 points to one gas only.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$M_r = \frac{m}{n} = \frac{0.68}{0.00810} \approx 84 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$$

options.A: Argon has $A_r \approx 39.9$. That would give a mass of only about $0.00810 \times 40 \approx 0.32 \text{ g}$ under these conditions, far less than the observed $0.68 \text{ g}$.
options.B: Krypton has $A_r \approx 83.8$. This matches the calculated $M_r \approx 84 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ perfectly, so the $0.68 \text{ g}$ sample corresponds to about $0.0081 \text{ mol}$ of krypton.
options.C: Neon has $A_r \approx 20.2$. That would give a mass of only about $0.00810 \times 20.2 \approx 0.16 \text{ g}$, much lighter than measured. Students who invert the $M_r$ calculation sometimes pick a light gas.
options.D: Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, has $M_r \approx 28.0$. That would give a mass of about $0.00810 \times 28 \approx 0.23 \text{ g}$, not $0.68 \text{ g}$. It is a common trap if you forget to convert $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$.
